business_problem: Kuken's engineers needed to find the correct replacement-part drawing in a 70-year archive. Even after digitization, searches depended on knowing historic part names and numbers, consuming experienced engineers' time and limiting newer staff's independence.
solution_summary: Kuken and Japanese AI startup Recursive built a drawing-search system and field app using OpenAI models through the OpenAI API. Engineers can enter a part or drawing number, or upload an image or PDF of a drawing or parts list. The app reads part numbers from the image or document and returns possible matches from Kuken's digitized archive, including drawings for similar designs. Engineers then compare the matched drawing with equipment specifications and replacement records to select the correct version for a customer installation. The system gives less experienced engineers a self-service way to find and study historic designs, while experienced staff gain more time for mentoring and engineering work. The source does not identify a specific model, archive-storage product, or retrieval infrastructure.

solution_components.name: OpenAI API
solution_components.role: Provides models that read drawing and parts-list details and support search within the engineering archive.

solution_components.name: Kuken drawing-search app
solution_components.role: Accepts part numbers, images, and PDFs and returns candidate historic drawings to field engineers.

data_flow: An engineer enters a part number or uploads a drawing or parts-list image/PDF; the app extracts part numbers, searches Kuken's digitized archive, and returns candidate drawings for the engineer to verify against installation specifications.
integration_points: Kuken's digitized archive of engineering drawings
Field engineers' image and PDF uploads
business_outcome: The search tool reduces drawing retrieval from nearly an hour to 4.5 minutes and is expected to cut annual search hours by about 90%. Newer engineers can handle a wider range of work independently, while experienced engineers spend more time mentoring.
metrics: 4.5 minutes to find a drawing, down from nearly an hour
Projected 90% reduction in hours spent searching for drawings each year
About 90% of issues flagged by the drawing-review prototype were genuine discrepancies
architecture_clues: Engineers can search by part/drawing number or upload an image or PDF
OpenAI models were compared for extraction accuracy and cost
A separate drawing-review tool remains in development and is not included as a deployed capability
